drivingQuestion: Why not let the condemned clear himself?

segments.he: אִם אֵינוֹ יוֹדֵעַ לְהִתְוַודּוֹת כּוּ׳. רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר כּוּ׳. לְנַקּוֹת עַצְמָן, וִינַקּוּ עַצְמָן! כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא לְהוֹצִיא לַעַז עַל בָּתֵּי דִינִין וְעַל הָעֵדִים.
segments.en: § The mishna teaches that «if» the condemned man «does not know how to confess,» they say to him: Say simply: Let my death be an atonement for all my sins. «Rabbi Yehuda says» that if he knows that he was wrongfully convicted, he should say: Let my death be an atonement for all my sins except for this sin. The Sages counter that if such a confession is acceptable, anyone who is sentenced to execution would state it «to clear himself» in the eyes of the public. The Gemara challenges: «Let them clear themselves.» Why should the court intervene if the condemned man wishes to proclaim his innocence? The Gemara answers: They intervene «so as not to cast aspersions on the courts and on the witnesses» who testified against him.
